    difficulty: hard
    category: [cross-stack]
    question: >-

    answer_format: "mechanism; path"

    difficulty: hard
    category: [calls, impact]
    question: >-
      What background workers/runners does the server actually START, and what drives

    difficulty: hard

addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- Explore: Fast read-only search agent for locating code. Use it to find files by pattern (eg. "src/components/**/*.tsx"), grep for symbols or keywords (eg. "API endpoints"), or answer "where is X defined / which files reference Y." Do NOT use it for code review, design-doc auditing, cross-file consistency checks, or open-ended analysis — it reads excerpts rather than whole files and will miss content past its read window. When calling, specify search breadth: "quick" for a single targeted lookup, "medium" for moderate exploration, or "very thorough" to search across multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

attachment.content:
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

package store

import (
	"context"
	"database/sql"
)

// Driver is an interface for store driver.
// It contains all methods that store database driver should implement.
type Driver interface {
	GetDB() *sql.DB
	Close() error

	IsInitialized(ctx context.Context) (bool, error)

	// GetDatabaseSize returns the database size in bytes, or -1 if unavailable.
	// A non-nil error indicates a hard failure; -1 with nil error means the
	// driver cannot report a size from the underlying database.
	GetDatabaseSize(ctx context.Context) (int64, error)

	// Attachment model related methods.
	CreateAttachment(ctx context.Context, create *Attachment) (*Attachment, error)
	ListAttachments(ctx context.Context, find *FindAttachment) ([]*Attachment, error)
	UpdateAttachment(ctx context.Context, update *UpdateAttachment) error
	DeleteAttachment(ctx context.Context, delete *DeleteAttachment) error
	DeleteAttachments(ctx context.Context, deletes []*DeleteAttachment) error

	// Memo model related methods.
	CreateMemo(ctx context.Context, create *Memo) (*Memo, error)
	ListMemos(ctx context.Context, find *FindMemo) ([]*Memo, error)
	UpdateMemo(ctx context.Context, update *UpdateMemo) error
	DeleteMemo(ctx context.Context, delete *DeleteMemo) error

	// MemoRelation model related methods.
	UpsertMemoRelation(ctx context.Context, create *MemoRelation) (*MemoRelation, error)
	ListMemoRelations(ctx context.Context, find *FindMemoRelation) ([]*MemoRelation, error)
	DeleteMemoRelation(ctx context.Context, delete *DeleteMemoRelation) error

	// InstanceSetting model related methods.
	UpsertInstanceSetting(ctx context.Context, upsert *InstanceSetting) (*InstanceSetting, error)
	ListInstanceSettings(ctx context.Context, find *FindInstanceSetting) ([]*InstanceSetting, error)
	DeleteInstanceSetting(ctx context.Context, delete *DeleteInstanceSetting) error

	// User model related methods.
	CreateUser(ctx context.Context, create *User) (*User, error)
	UpdateUser(ctx context.Context, update *UpdateUser) (*User, error)
	ListUsers(ctx context.Context, find *FindUser) ([]*User, error)
	DeleteUser(ctx context.Context, delete *DeleteUser) (*DeleteUserResult, error)

	// UserSetting model related methods.
	UpsertUserSetting(ctx context.Context, upsert *UserSetting) (*UserSetting, error)
	ListUserSettings(ctx context.Context, find *FindUserSetting) ([]*UserSetting, error)
	DeleteUserSettings(ctx context.Context, delete *DeleteUserSetting) error
	GetUserByPATHash(ctx context.Context, tokenHash string) (*PATQueryResult, error)

	// IdentityProvider model related methods.
	CreateIdentityProvider(ctx context.Context, create *IdentityProvider) (*IdentityProvider, error)
	ListIdentityProviders(ctx context.Context, find *FindIdentityProvider) ([]*IdentityProvider, error)
	UpdateIdentityProvider(ctx context.Context, update *UpdateIdentityProvider) (*IdentityProvider, error)
	DeleteIdentityProvider(ctx context.Context, delete *DeleteIdentityProvider) error
	ApplyAuthenticationConfigMutation(ctx context.Context, mutation *AuthenticationConfigMutation) error
	IsRetryableAuthenticationMutationError(err error) bool

	// Inbox model related methods.
	CreateInbox(ctx context.Context, create *Inbox) (*Inbox, error)
	ListInboxes(ctx context.Context, find *FindInbox) ([]*Inbox, error)
	UpdateInbox(ctx context.Context, update *UpdateInbox) (*Inbox, error)
	DeleteInbox(ctx context.Context, delete *DeleteInbox) error

	// Reaction model related methods.
	UpsertReaction(ctx context.Context, create *Reaction) (*Reaction, error)
	ListReactions(ctx context.Context, find *FindReaction) ([]*Reaction, error)
	GetReaction(ctx context.Context, find *FindReaction) (*Reaction, error)
	DeleteReaction(ctx context.Context, delete *DeleteReaction) error

	// MemoShare model related methods.
	CreateMemoShare(ctx context.Context, create *MemoShare) (*MemoShare, error)
	ListMemoShares(ctx context.Context, find *FindMemoShare) ([]*MemoShare, error)
	GetMemoShare(ctx context.Context, find *FindMemoShare) (*MemoShare, error)
	DeleteMemoShare(ctx context.Context, delete *DeleteMemoShare) error

	// UserIdentity model related methods.
	CreateUserIdentity(ctx context.Context, create *UserIdentity) (*UserIdentity, error)
	ListUserIdentities(ctx context.Context, find *FindUserIdentity) ([]*UserIdentity, error)
	DeleteUserIdentities(ctx context.Context, delete *DeleteUserIdentity) error
}

3	import (
4		"context"
5		"fmt"

8		"net/http"
9		"os"
10		"sync"
11		"time"

13		"github.com/google/uuid"
14		"github.com/labstack/echo/v5"
15		"github.com/labstack/echo/v5/middleware"
16		"github.com/pkg/errors"
17	
18		"github.com/usememos/memos/internal/profile"
19		storepb "github.com/usememos/memos/proto/gen/store"
20		apiv1 "github.com/usememos/memos/server/router/api/v1"
21		"github.com/usememos/memos/server/router/fileserver"
22		"github.com/usememos/memos/server/router/frontend"
23		"github.com/usememos/memos/server/router/mcp"
24		"github.com/usememos/memos/server/router/rss"
25		"github.com/usememos/memos/server/runner/s3presign"
26		"github.com/usememos/memos/store"
27	)
28	
29	const shutdownTimeout = 10 * time.Second
30	
31	type Server struct {
32		Secret  string
33		Profile *profile.Profile
34		Store   *store.Store
35	
36		echoServer *echo.Echo
37		httpServer *http.Server
38		sseHub     *apiv1.SSEHub
39	
40		backgroundRunnerCancels []context.CancelFunc
41		backgroundRunnerWG      sync.WaitGroup
42	}
43	
44	func NewServer(ctx context.Context, profile *profile.Profile, store *store.Store) (*Server, error) {
45		s := &Server{
46			Store:   store,
47			Profile: profile,
48		}
49	
50		echoServer := echo.New()
51		echoServer.Use(middleware.Recover())
52		echoServer.Use(newCORSMiddleware(profile))
53		s.echoServer = echoServer
54	
55		instanceBasicSetting, err := s.getOrUpsertInstanceBasicSetting(ctx)
56		if err != nil {
57			return nil, errors.Wrap(err, "failed to get instance basic setting")
58		}
59	
60		secret := "usememos"
61		if !profile.Demo {
62			secret = instanceBasicSetting.SecretKey
63		}
64		s.Secret = secret
65	
66		// Register healthz endpoint.
67		echoServer.GET("/healthz", func(c *echo.Context) error {
68			return c.String(http.StatusOK, "Service ready.")
69		})
70	
71		// Serve frontend static files.
72		frontend.NewFrontendService(profile, store).Serve(ctx, echoServer)
73	
74		rootGroup := echoServer.Group("")
75	
76		apiV1Service := apiv1.NewAPIV1Service(s.Secret, profile, store)
77		s.sseHub = apiV1Service.SSEHub
78	
79		// Register HTTP file server routes BEFORE gRPC-Gateway to ensure proper range request handling for Safari.
80		// This uses native HTTP serving (http.ServeContent) instead of gRPC for video/audio files.
81		fileServerService := fileserver.NewFileServerService(s.Profile, s.Store, s.Secret)
82		fileServerService.RegisterRoutes(echoServer)
83	
84		// Create and register RSS routes (needs markdown service from apiV1Service).
85		rss.NewRSSService(s.Profile, s.Store, apiV1Service.MarkdownService).RegisterRoutes(rootGroup)
86	
87		// Register gRPC gateway as api v1 (includes SSE endpoint on CORS-enabled group).
88		if err := apiV1Service.RegisterGateway(ctx, echoServer); err != nil {
89			return nil, errors.Wrap(err, "failed to register gRPC gateway")
90		}
91	
92		mcpService, err := mcp.NewMCPService(profile, echoServer)
93		if err != nil {
94			return nil, errors.Wrap(err, "failed to create MCP service")
95		}
96		mcpService.RegisterRoutes(echoServer)
97	
98		return s, nil
99	}
100	
101	func (s *Server) Start(ctx context.Context) error {
102		var address, network string
103		if len(s.Profile.UNIXSock) == 0 {
104			address = fmt.Sprintf("%s:%d", s.Profile.Addr, s.Profile.Port)
105			network = "tcp"
106		} else {
107			address = s.Profile.UNIXSock
108			network = "unix"
109		}
110		listener, err := net.Listen(network, address)
111		if err != nil {
112			return errors.Wrap(err, "failed to listen")
113		}
114	
115		if network == "unix" {
116			if err := os.Chmod(address, 0660); err != nil {
117				_ = listener.Close()
118				return errors.Wrap(err, "failed to chmod socket")
119			}
120		}
121	
122		// Start Echo server directly (no cmux needed - all traffic is HTTP).
123		s.httpServer = &http.Server{Handler: s.echoServer}
124		go func() {
125			if err := s.httpServer.Serve(listener); err != nil && err != http.ErrServerClosed {
126				slog.Error("failed to start echo server", "error", err)
127			}
128		}()
129		s.startBackgroundRunners(ctx)
130	
131		return nil
132	}
133	
134	func (s *Server) Shutdown(ctx context.Context) {
135		ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, shutdownTimeout)
136		defer cancel()
137	
138		slog.Info("server shutting down")
139	
140		s.stopBackgroundRunners()
141		s.closeLongLivedConnections()
142		s.shutdownHTTPServer(ctx)
143		s.waitBackgroundRunners(ctx)
144	
145		// Close database connection.
146		if err := s.Store.Close(); err != nil {

154		// Create a separate context for each background runner
155		// This allows us to control cancellation for each runner independently

166		s.backgroundRunnerWG.Add(1)
167		go func() {

170			slog.Info("s3presign runner stopped")
171		}()
172	
173		slog.Info("background runners started")
174	}

176	func (s *Server) stopBackgroundRunners() {
177		for _, cancelFunc := range s.backgroundRunnerCancels {
178			if cancelFunc != nil {

180			}
181		}
182	}

185		done := make(chan struct{})

189		}()
190	
191		select {
192		case <-done:
193		case <-ctx.Done():

195			case <-done:

198			}

65	func (s *APIV1Service) RegisterGateway(ctx context.Context, echoServer *echo.Echo) error {

67		// policy, used by both the gRPC-Gateway middleware and the Connect interceptor.
68		authorizer := NewAuthorizer(s.Store, s.Secret, s.Profile)
69		gatewayAuthMiddleware := func(next runtime.HandlerFunc) runtime.HandlerFunc {
70			return func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request, pathParams map[string]string) {
71				ctx := r.Context()
72	
73				// The RPC method name is set by grpc-gateway after routing. When it can't be
74				// determined, skip the policy check and let the service layer handle visibility.
75				rpcMethod, ok := runtime.RPCMethod(ctx)
76				authHeader := r.Header.Get("Authorization")
77	
78				result := authorizer.Authenticate(ctx, authHeader)
79				if ok {

81						http.Error(w, `{"code": 16, "message": "authentication required"}`, http.StatusUnauthorized)
82						return
83					}
84				}
85	
86				// Apply the identity to the context (no-op for permitted anonymous requests).
87				if result != nil {
88					r = r.WithContext(auth.ApplyToContext(ctx, result))
89				}
90	
91				next(w, r, pathParams)
92			}
93		}
94	
95		// Create gRPC-Gateway mux with auth middleware.
96		gwMux := runtime.NewServeMux(
97			runtime.WithMiddlewares(gatewayAuthMiddleware),
98		)
99		if err := v1pb.RegisterInstanceServiceHandlerServer(ctx, gwMux, s); err != nil {
100			return err
101		}
102		if err := v1pb.RegisterAuthServiceHandlerServer(ctx, gwMux, s); err != nil {
103			return err
104		}
105		if err := v1pb.RegisterUserServiceHandlerServer(ctx, gwMux, s); err != nil {
106			return err

109			return err

112			return err
113		}

115			return err
116		}
117		if err := v1pb.RegisterShortcutServiceHandlerServer(ctx, gwMux, s); err != nil {
118			return err
119		}
120		if err := v1pb.RegisterIdentityProviderServiceHandlerServer(ctx, gwMux, s); err != nil {
121			return err
122		}
123		gwGroup := echoServer.Group("")
124		// Register SSE endpoint with same CORS as rest of /api/v1.
125		RegisterSSERoutes(gwGroup, s.SSEHub, s.Store, s.Secret)
126		handler := echo.WrapHandler(http.MaxBytesHandler(gwMux, maxAPIRequestBytes))
127	
128		gwGroup.Any("/api/v1/*", handler)
129		gwGroup.Any("/file/*", handler)
130	
131		// Connect handlers for browser clients (replaces grpc-web).
132		logStacktraces := s.Profile.Demo
133		connectInterceptors := connect.WithInterceptors(
134			NewMetadataInterceptor(), // Convert HTTP headers to gRPC metadata first
135			NewLoggingInterceptor(logStacktraces),
136			NewRecoveryInterceptor(logStacktraces),
137			NewAuthInterceptor(authorizer),
138		)
139		connectMux := http.NewServeMux()
140		connectHandler := NewConnectServiceHandler(s)
141		connectHandler.RegisterConnectHandlers(connectMux, connectInterceptors, connect.WithReadMaxBytes(maxAPIRequestBytes))
142	
143		connectGroup := echoServer.Group("")
144		connectGroup.Any("/memos.api.v1.*", echo.WrapHandler(http.MaxBytesHandler(connectMux, maxAPIRequestBytes)))
145	
146		return nil
147	}

In `runner.go` (lines 29-41), `Run()` creates a `time.NewTicker` with a 12-hour interval (`runnerInterval = time.Hour * 12`) and calls `RunOnce` each tick. `RunOnce` calls `CheckAndPresign`, which iterates over all S3-type attachments in batches of 100, checks whether their pre-signed URL is about to expire (within 4 days of a 5-day expiration window), and generates fresh pre-signed URLs via the S3 client.

**What it does:** Periodically (every 12 hours) refreshes pre-signed S3 URLs for all S3-backed attachments, ensuring they remain accessible. Also runs once immediately at server startup.

This runner is tracked via `backgroundRunnerCancels` (line 40) and `backgroundRunnerWG` (line 41) on the `Server` struct, and is cleanly shut down during `Shutdown()` (lines 140, 143).

<result>Here is the complete picture of how frontend API requests are authenticated:

---

## Authentication Architecture

### 1. Token Storage: `/bench/repo/web/src/auth-state.ts`

This module manages the access token lifecycle:

- **In-memory state**: `accessToken` (string) and `tokenExpiresAt` (Date) are held as module-level variables.
- **Persistent storage**: Tokens are persisted to `localStorage` under keys `memos_access_token` and `memos_token_expires_at`.
- **Cross-tab sync**: A `BroadcastChannel` named `memos_token_sync` is created at module load (line 50). When one tab refreshes a token, it broadcasts a `TokenBroadcastMessage` (`{ token, expiresAt }`) so other tabs adopt the new token without making their own refresh calls.
- **Key exports**:
  - `getAccessToken()` (line 52): Returns the in-memory token, falling back to `localStorage` if not yet loaded. Expired tokens in storage are intentionally NOT removed here (to allow the refresh flow to work).
  - `setAccessToken(token, expiresAt)` (line 78): Stores token in memory + `localStorage` and broadcasts to other tabs.
  - `isTokenExpired(bufferMs)` (line 99): Returns true if the token will expire within `bufferMs` (default 30s).
  - `hasStoredToken()` (line 109): Checks if any token exists in localStorage (even expired), used to decide whether to attempt a refresh.
  - `clearAccessToken()` (line 118): Wipes token from memory and `localStorage`.
- **Two expiry buffer constants**: `REQUEST_TOKEN_EXPIRY_BUFFER_MS = 30s` (for normal API calls) and `FOCUS_TOKEN_EXPIRY_BUFFER_MS = 2min` (for proactive refresh on tab focus).

### 2. ConnectRPC Transport & Auth Interceptor: `/bench/repo/web/src/connect.ts`

This is the core wiring. It uses `@connectrpc/connect-web` with `createConnectTransport`.

**Token Refresh Manager** (lines 30-49): A singleton that deduplicates concurrent refresh requests. If a refresh is already in flight, subsequent callers await the same promise.

**Refresh Transport** (lines 64-72): A *separate* transport with `interceptors: []` (no auth interceptor) is used exclusively for the `AuthService.refreshToken` RPC. This prevents recursion -- the refresh call itself uses `credentials: "include"` (sending cookies) rather than a Bearer token.

**`doRefreshAccessToken()`** (line 74): Calls `refreshAuthClient.refreshToken({})`, extracts `response.accessToken` and `response.expiresAt`, and saves them via `setAccessToken()`.

**`getRequestToken()`** (lines 124-150): The pre-flight token resolution logic:
1. Gets the current in-memory/localStorage token.
2. If no token exists and no token was ever stored, returns `null` (unauthenticated request).
3. If a stored token exists but the in-memory one is missing, triggers a refresh attempt.
4. If the token is about to expire (within 30s buffer), proactively refreshes it before sending the request.

**`authInterceptor`** (lines 156-178): The ConnectRPC `Interceptor` that authenticates every API request:
1. Calls `getRequestToken()` to get a (possibly refreshed) token.
2. Sets the `Authorization: Bearer <token>` header via `setAuthorizationHeader()` (line 97-100).
3. Sends the request via `next(req)`.
4. On **`Code.Unauthenticated` (401)** error:
   - If this is NOT already a retry (checked via `X-Retry` header), it attempts a token refresh, sets the new token, marks the request with `X-Retry: true`, and retries.
   - If the retry also fails, calls `redirectOnAuthFailure()` and rethrows.

**Main Transport** (lines 184-189): All service clients use this transport:
```typescript
const transport = createConnectTransport({
  baseUrl: window.location.origin,
  useBinaryFormat: true,
  fetch: fetchWithCredentials,    // credentials: "include" for cookies
  interceptors: [authInterceptor],
});
```

**Service clients** (lines 192-204): Eight clients are created on this transport:
- `instanceServiceClient`, `authServiceClient`, `userServiceClient`
- `memoServiceClient`, `attachmentServiceClient`, `aiServiceClient`, `shortcutServiceClient`
- `identityProviderServiceClient`

### 3. Proactive Token Refresh on Tab Focus: `/bench/repo/web/src/hooks/useTokenRefreshOnFocus.ts`

A React hook that listens for `visibilitychange` events. When the tab becomes visible and the token is expired or expiring within 2 minutes (`FOCUS_TOKEN_EXPIRY_BUFFER_MS`), it proactively calls `refreshAccessToken()`. This runs before React Query's refetch-on-window-focus, preventing cascading 401 errors. Wired up in `/bench/repo/web/src/main.tsx` at line 46.

### 4. Auth Failure Redirect: `/bench/repo/web/src/utils/auth-redirect.ts`

When the interceptor's retry fails, `redirectOnAuthFailure()` (line 27):
1. No-ops if already on an auth page.
2. No-ops if on a public route (unless `forceRedirect` is set).
3. Calls `clearAccessToken()` to wipe credentials.
4. Redirects to the auth page via `window.location.replace()`, preserving the current URL as a redirect target.

### 5. OAuth / PKCE Support: `/bench/repo/web/src/utils/oauth.ts`

Handles the OAuth authorization flow with CSRF protection (random state parameter stored in `sessionStorage`) and optional PKCE (`code_verifier` / `code_challenge` using SHA-256). This is for the initial sign-in via external identity providers, not for ongoing API auth.

---

### Summary of the request authentication flow:

## ListMemos Filter Expression Parsing: Complete Analysis

### Syntax/Engine

The filter uses **Google CEL (Common Expression Language)** via the `github.com/google/cel-go` library, version **0.28.1** (from `go.mod`). Filter strings are standard CEL syntax, not a custom grammar.

### Architecture Overview

The filter engine lives in a self-contained package at `/bench/repo/internal/filter/` and follows a three-phase pipeline:

1. **CEL Parsing** (via `cel-go`) -- the raw string is compiled into a CEL AST
2. **Normalization** -- the CEL AST is transformed into a dialect-agnostic intermediate representation (IR)
3. **Rendering** -- the IR tree is walked to produce SQL fragments for the target database dialect (SQLite, MySQL, or Postgres)

1	# Memo Filter Engine
2	
3	This package houses the memo-only filter engine that turns standard CEL syntax
4	into SQL fragments for the subset of expressions supported by the memo schema.
5	The engine follows a three phase pipeline inspired by systems
6	such as Calcite or Prisma:
7	
8	1. **Parsing** – CEL expressions are parsed with `cel-go` and validated against
9	   the memo-specific environment declared in `schema.go`. Only fields that
10	   exist in the schema can surface in the filter, and non-standard legacy
11	   coercions are rejected.
12	2. **Normalization** – the raw CEL AST is converted into an intermediate
13	   representation (IR) defined in `ir.go`. The IR is a dialect-agnostic tree of
14	   conditions (logical operators, comparisons, list membership, etc.). This
15	   step enforces schema rules (e.g. operator compatibility, type checks).
16	3. **Rendering** – the renderer in `render.go` walks the IR and produces a SQL
17	   fragment plus placeholder arguments tailored to a target dialect
18	   (`sqlite`, `mysql`, or `postgres`). Dialect differences such as JSON access,
19	   boolean semantics, placeholders, and `LIKE` vs `ILIKE` are encapsulated in
20	   renderer helpers.
21	
22	The entry point is `filter.DefaultEngine()` from `engine.go`. It lazily constructs
23	an `Engine` configured with the memo schema and exposes:
24	
25	```go
26	engine, _ := filter.DefaultEngine()
27	stmt, _ := engine.CompileToStatement(ctx, `has_task_list && visibility == "PUBLIC"`, filter.RenderOptions{
28		Dialect: filter.DialectPostgres,
29	})
30	// stmt.SQL  -> "((memo.payload->'property'->>'hasTaskList')::boolean IS TRUE AND memo.visibility = $1)"
31	// stmt.Args -> ["PUBLIC"]
32	```
33	
34	## Core Files
35	
36	| File          | Responsibility                                                                  |
37	| ------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
38	| `schema.go`   | Declares memo fields, their types, backing columns, CEL environment options     |
39	| `ir.go`       | IR node definitions used across the pipeline                                    |
40	| `parser.go`   | Converts CEL `Expr` into IR while applying schema validation                    |
41	| `render.go`   | Translates IR into SQL, handling dialect-specific behavior                      |
42	| `engine.go`   | Glue between the phases; exposes `Compile`, `CompileToStatement`, and `DefaultEngine` |
43	| `helpers.go`  | Convenience helpers for store integration (appending conditions)                |
44	
45	## SQL Generation Notes
46	
47	- **Placeholders** — `?` is used for SQLite/MySQL, `$n` for Postgres. The renderer
48	  tracks offsets to compose queries with pre-existing arguments.
49	- **JSON Fields** — Memo metadata lives in `memo.payload`. The renderer handles
50	  `JSON_EXTRACT`/`json_extract`/`->`/`->>` variations and boolean coercion.
51	- **Time Fields** — `created_ts`, `updated_ts`, and attachment `create_time` are
52	  CEL `timestamp` values. Express instants with the `now` variable,
53	  `duration("…")` (e.g. `created_ts >= now - duration("24h")`), or
54	  `timestamp("2006-01-02T15:04:05Z")` / `timestamp(<epoch-seconds>)`. These fold
55	  to epoch seconds at compile time — `now` is frozen once per compile (injectable
56	  for tests via the engine clock) — so the backing columns stay unchanged.
57	- **Tag Operations** — `tag in [...]` and `"tag" in tags` become JSON array
58	  predicates. SQLite uses `LIKE` patterns, MySQL uses `JSON_CONTAINS`, and
59	  Postgres uses `@>`.
60	- **Boolean Flags** — Fields such as `has_task_list` render as `IS TRUE` equality
61	  checks, or comparisons against `CAST('true' AS JSON)` depending on the dialect.
62	- **String Matching** — `content.contains(x)`, `content.startsWith(x)`, and
63	  `content.endsWith(x)` render as case-insensitive `LIKE`/`ILIKE` with LIKE
64	  metacharacters (`%`, `_`, `\`) escaped. Available on scalar string fields whose
65	  schema sets `SupportsContains` (memo `content`; attachment `filename`,
66	  `mime_type`).
67	- **Regex** — `field.matches("pattern")` renders to `~` (Postgres) or `REGEXP`
68	  (MySQL/SQLite). SQLite uses a Go-backed `regexp` function registered in
69	  `store/db/sqlite/functions.go`. Patterns are validated at compile time against
70	  Go's RE2 via `cel.ValidateRegexLiterals()`. **Caveat:** regex *syntax* differs
71	  per engine (Go RE2 on SQLite, POSIX ERE on Postgres, ICU on MySQL 8.0+), so
72	  engine-specific patterns may not be portable.
73	- **Tag `all()` / `exists_one()`** — `tags.all(t, <pred>)` matches only non-empty
74	  tag sets where every element satisfies the predicate; `tags.exists_one(t,
75	  <pred>)` matches when exactly one element does (`COUNT(...) = 1`). Both iterate
76	  per-element (`json_each` / `jsonb_array_elements_text` / `JSON_TABLE`).
77	- **Timestamp Accessors** — `created_ts.getFullYear()`, `getMonth()`, `getDate()`,
78	  `getDayOfMonth()`, `getDayOfWeek()`, `getDayOfYear()`, `getHours()`,
79	  `getMinutes()`, `getSeconds()` render to date-part extraction (`strftime` /
80	  `EXTRACT` / `YEAR`/`MONTH`/…). Results are normalized to CEL's base (0-based
81	  month, 0-based day-of-week with 0 = Sunday). The same accessors on `now` fold
82	  to literal date parts of the frozen evaluation time (UTC), so saved filters
83	  like `created_ts.getMonth() == now.getMonth() && created_ts.getDate() ==
84	  now.getDate()` ("on this day") re-resolve on every compile. Extraction is UTC
85	  on SQLite/Postgres (epoch columns); on MySQL the `TIMESTAMP` column is read in
86	  the session time zone. A timezone argument is not supported.
87	- **Set Operations** — `ext.Sets()`: `sets.contains(tags, [...])`,
88	  `sets.intersects(tags, [...])`, and `sets.equivalent(tags, [...])` desugar to
89	  exact-membership checks (AND / OR of `"v" in tags`); `equivalent` adds a
90	  `size(tags)` length check (relies on tags being a set).
91	- **`size()`** — `size(tags)` renders to JSON array length; `size(content)` (and
92	  other string fields) render to `LENGTH` / `CHAR_LENGTH` (MySQL) for code-point
93	  counts.
94	- **Arithmetic** — `+`, `-`, `*`, `/`, `%` constant-fold on literal/`now`/`duration`
95	  operands (division and modulo guard against a zero divisor).
96	
97	## Typical Integration
98	
99	1. Fetch the engine with `filter.DefaultEngine()`.
100	2. Call `CompileToStatement` using the appropriate dialect enum.
101	3. Append the emitted SQL fragment/args to the existing `WHERE` clause.
102	4. Execute the resulting query through the store driver.
103	
104	The `helpers.AppendConditions` helper encapsulates steps 2–3 when a driver needs
105	to process an array of filters.

# Memo Filter Engine

This package houses the memo-only filter engine that turns standard CEL syntax
into SQL fragments for the subset of expressions supported by the memo schema.
The engine follows a three phase pipeline inspired by systems
such as Calcite or Prisma:

1. **Parsing** – CEL expressions are parsed with `cel-go` and validated against
   the memo-specific environment declared in `schema.go`. Only fields that
   exist in the schema can surface in the filter, and non-standard legacy
   coercions are rejected.
2. **Normalization** – the raw CEL AST is converted into an intermediate
   representation (IR) defined in `ir.go`. The IR is a dialect-agnostic tree of
   conditions (logical operators, comparisons, list membership, etc.). This
   step enforces schema rules (e.g. operator compatibility, type checks).
3. **Rendering** – the renderer in `render.go` walks the IR and produces a SQL
   fragment plus placeholder arguments tailored to a target dialect
   (`sqlite`, `mysql`, or `postgres`). Dialect differences such as JSON access,
   boolean semantics, placeholders, and `LIKE` vs `ILIKE` are encapsulated in
   renderer helpers.

The entry point is `filter.DefaultEngine()` from `engine.go`. It lazily constructs
an `Engine` configured with the memo schema and exposes:

```go
engine, _ := filter.DefaultEngine()
stmt, _ := engine.CompileToStatement(ctx, `has_task_list && visibility == "PUBLIC"`, filter.RenderOptions{
	Dialect: filter.DialectPostgres,
})
// stmt.SQL  -> "((memo.payload->'property'->>'hasTaskList')::boolean IS TRUE AND memo.visibility = $1)"
// stmt.Args -> ["PUBLIC"]
```

## Core Files

| File          | Responsibility                                                                  |
| ------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `schema.go`   | Declares memo fields, their types, backing columns, CEL environment options     |
| `ir.go`       | IR node definitions used across the pipeline                                    |
| `parser.go`   | Converts CEL `Expr` into IR while applying schema validation                    |
| `render.go`   | Translates IR into SQL, handling dialect-specific behavior                      |
| `engine.go`   | Glue between the phases; exposes `Compile`, `CompileToStatement`, and `DefaultEngine` |
| `helpers.go`  | Convenience helpers for store integration (appending conditions)                |

## SQL Generation Notes

- **Placeholders** — `?` is used for SQLite/MySQL, `$n` for Postgres. The renderer
  tracks offsets to compose queries with pre-existing arguments.
- **JSON Fields** — Memo metadata lives in `memo.payload`. The renderer handles
  `JSON_EXTRACT`/`json_extract`/`->`/`->>` variations and boolean coercion.
- **Time Fields** — `created_ts`, `updated_ts`, and attachment `create_time` are
  CEL `timestamp` values. Express instants with the `now` variable,
  `duration("…")` (e.g. `created_ts >= now - duration("24h")`), or
  `timestamp("2006-01-02T15:04:05Z")` / `timestamp(<epoch-seconds>)`. These fold
  to epoch seconds at compile time — `now` is frozen once per compile (injectable
  for tests via the engine clock) — so the backing columns stay unchanged.
- **Tag Operations** — `tag in [...]` and `"tag" in tags` become JSON array
  predicates. SQLite uses `LIKE` patterns, MySQL uses `JSON_CONTAINS`, and
  Postgres uses `@>`.
- **Boolean Flags** — Fields such as `has_task_list` render as `IS TRUE` equality
  checks, or comparisons against `CAST('true' AS JSON)` depending on the dialect.
- **String Matching** — `content.contains(x)`, `content.startsWith(x)`, and
  `content.endsWith(x)` render as case-insensitive `LIKE`/`ILIKE` with LIKE
  metacharacters (`%`, `_`, `\`) escaped. Available on scalar string fields whose
  schema sets `SupportsContains` (memo `content`; attachment `filename`,

- **Regex** — `field.matches("pattern")` renders to `~` (Postgres) or `REGEXP`
  (MySQL/SQLite). SQLite uses a Go-backed `regexp` function registered in
  `store/db/sqlite/functions.go`. Patterns are validated at compile time against
  Go's RE2 via `cel.ValidateRegexLiterals()`. **Caveat:** regex *syntax* differs
  per engine (Go RE2 on SQLite, POSIX ERE on Postgres, ICU on MySQL 8.0+), so
  engine-specific patterns may not be portable.
- **Tag `all()` / `exists_one()`** — `tags.all(t, <pred>)` matches only non-empty
  tag sets where every element satisfies the predicate; `tags.exists_one(t,
  <pred>)` matches when exactly one element does (`COUNT(...) = 1`). Both iterate
  per-element (`json_each` / `jsonb_array_elements_text` / `JSON_TABLE`).
- **Timestamp Accessors** — `created_ts.getFullYear()`, `getMonth()`, `getDate()`,
  `getDayOfMonth()`, `getDayOfWeek()`, `getDayOfYear()`, `getHours()`,
  `getMinutes()`, `getSeconds()` render to date-part extraction (`strftime` /
  `EXTRACT` / `YEAR`/`MONTH`/…). Results are normalized to CEL's base (0-based
  month, 0-based day-of-week with 0 = Sunday). The same accessors on `now` fold
  to literal date parts of the frozen evaluation time (UTC), so saved filters
  like `created_ts.getMonth() == now.getMonth() && created_ts.getDate() ==
  now.getDate()` ("on this day") re-resolve on every compile. Extraction is UTC
  on SQLite/Postgres (epoch columns); on MySQL the `TIMESTAMP` column is read in
  the session time zone. A timezone argument is not supported.
- **Set Operations** — `ext.Sets()`: `sets.contains(tags, [...])`,
  `sets.intersects(tags, [...])`, and `sets.equivalent(tags, [...])` desugar to

1	package v1

3	import (
4		"strings"
5	
6		"github.com/pkg/errors"

9	)
10	
11	func (*APIV1Service) parseMemoOrderBy(orderBy string, memoFind *store.FindMemo) error {
12		if strings.TrimSpace(orderBy) == "" {
13			return errors.New("empty order_by")
14		}
15	
16		// Split by comma to support multiple sort fields per AIP-132.
17		fields := strings.Split(orderBy, ",")
18	
19		// Track if we've seen pinned field.
20		hasPinned := false
21		hasExplicitTimeField := false
22	
23		for _, field := range fields {
24			parts := strings.Fields(strings.TrimSpace(field))
25			if len(parts) == 0 {
26				continue
27			}
28	
29			fieldName := parts[0]
30			fieldDirection := "desc" // default per AIP-132 (we use desc as default for time fields)
31			if len(parts) > 1 {
32				fieldDirection = strings.ToLower(parts[1])
33				if fieldDirection != "asc" && fieldDirection != "desc" {
34					return errors.Errorf("invalid order direction: %s, must be 'asc' or 'desc'", parts[1])
35				}
36			}
37	
38			switch fieldName {
39			case "pinned":
40				hasPinned = true
41				memoFind.OrderByPinned = true
42				// Note: pinned is always DESC (true first) regardless of direction specified.
43			case "create_time", "name":
44				// Only set if this is the first time field we encounter.
45				if !hasExplicitTimeField {
46					memoFind.OrderByTimeAsc = fieldDirection == "asc"
47				}
48				hasExplicitTimeField = true
49			case "update_time":
50				// Only set if this is the first time field we encounter.
51				if !hasExplicitTimeField {
52					memoFind.OrderByUpdatedTs = true
53					memoFind.OrderByTimeAsc = fieldDirection == "asc"
54				}
55				hasExplicitTimeField = true
56			default:
57				return errors.Errorf("unsupported order field: %s, supported fields are: pinned, create_time, update_time, name", fieldName)
58			}

2. **Normalization** -- the CEL AST is transformed into a dialect-agnostic intermediate representation (IR)
